answer: Gale-Priced Join Queue: agents entering the economy draw a random wait rank from a publicly verifiable seed; each new identity must let its rank elapse before transacting, and rank is re-drawn upward whenever a harbor of linked identities appears in the same queue window. An attacker flooding N sock puppets pays N times the queue-delay and, because clustering raises every raven’s rank, must also spend real compute to stagger arrivals. Coordination itself becomes the priced scarce good: honest lone agents wait briefly, while mass registration costs unbounded elapsed time per identity.
